# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4 (GGUF)

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf` keeps the routed experts of
[deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) exactly as DeepSeek
released them, in FP4, made by ELVEZ from the official weights. The official checkpoint stores the routed experts in
FP4 (E2M1 values with one E8M0 scale per 32 values); this file repacks those bytes into the GGUF MXFP4 layout without
changing any value. ELVEZ's [standard V4.1 Flash 1017 Q2](https://huggingface.co/elvezjp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-Q2-gguf)
instead quantizes the experts to about 2.3 bits.

On a Mac Studio (M3 Ultra, 512 GB) with the same engine and settings, this file scored **162/164 on HumanEval**
against 152/164 for the standard Q2, with Japanese QA and long-form writing equal or slightly better. Decode was
5–8% slower and the model needs about 287 GiB of memory instead of about 161 GiB.

This is a model that [IXV](https://ixv.jp/) — ELVEZ's AI development distribution for software development in Japan —
is trying on a Mac Studio as its main model. It is published here so that anyone can check how it was made and what
we measured.

This card records what we measured and what we have not. Everything here is as of 2026-11-11.

> **Runtime.** We have run this file only on IXV's engine (`ixv-server`), with Metal on an M3 Ultra. The GGUF
> stores the Engram tables in a layout of its own, so it is not a general-purpose GGUF. The llama.cpp, Ollama and
> other snippets in the "Use this model" menu are generated by Hugging Face for every GGUF; we have not tested any of
> them, and we do not expect them to work. See [Compatibility](#compatibility).

日本語の概要は[末尾](#日本語の概要)にあります。

## Files

The GGUF is larger than the Hub's 500 GB limit for a single file, so it is published in three parts. Download all
three and join them:

```sh
cat DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf.part1of3 \
    DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf.part2of3 \
    DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf.part3of3 > DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf
shasum -a 256 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf   # must print the SHA-256 below
```

| File | Size | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf` (joined) | 501,609,136,128 bytes | `2bcee3bc6fa73b18e0d5c50ac671af14ae7b480c1f8eab60d30fd0b1197d91e0` |
| `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf.part1of3` | 167,203,045,376 bytes | `05154551ab3dc7e983d2eab583ae88d73fafbac6e80d53aea8f0d539af952e18` |
| `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf.part2of3` | 167,203,045,376 bytes | `7adc072b6e23342302d36a17876924e86cfd1d8ef18baded18c641ac19a8a0eb` |
| `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf.part3of3` | 167,203,045,376 bytes | `0e5fc1d108863e98d060f0be4d30bf3c07a767dd67b904d55267c499c96d3f20` |

The parts are plain byte ranges of the joined file (`split`); they are not usable on their own. Joining needs about
467 GiB of free disk in addition to the parts.

The vision encoder (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Vision.gguf`) and the DSpark draft head
(`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-DSpark.gguf`) are the same files as in the
[standard repository](https://huggingface.co/elvezjp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-Q2-gguf) and are not repeated here.

## What is in the file

| Tensors | Type |
|---|---|
| Routed experts, gate, up and down | **MXFP4, the official FP4 values and E8M0 scales, unchanged** |
| Attention projections, shared experts, output head | Q8_0 (the official weights are FP8) |
| Norms, router and other small tensors | F16 / F32 as in the recipe |
| Engram tables | the official FP8 values and scales, unchanged, packed at the end of the file (188.8 GiB) |

- 1,046 tensors, the same layout as the standard Q2 except for the type of the routed experts (288,777,830,400 bytes
  of experts against 152,882,380,800 bytes in the Q2).
- No imatrix: nothing is recomputed in the experts, so there is nothing to calibrate.
- Only the non-expert matrices are converted (FP8 to Q8_0), as in the standard Q2.
- The main weights that stay in memory are about 278.3 GiB; the engine reads only the Engram rows it needs from disk.

## Provenance

| | |
|---|---|
| Base model | [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), revision `1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170` (recorded in the GGUF's `general.source.revision`), MIT license |
| Converter | IXV `tools/gguf/deepseek41_quantize.py --quant fp4`, written by ELVEZ on top of the converter imported from antirez/ds4 `gguf-tools` (MIT); the FP4 repack is the one IXV already used for the DSpark file |

## How it was made

```
deepseek41_quantize.py --hf DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --source-revision 1bae0e10… --quant fp4 --out DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf
deepseek41_validate_gguf.py --hf DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --source-revision 1bae0e10… --quant fp4 --payload --gguf DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-FP4.gguf
```

- Made from the official safetensors in about 17 minutes on the M3 Ultra (16 threads).
- Checked against the official weights: all 1,046 tensor layouts; every routed expert equals the repack of the
  official FP4 bytes, and the first and last expert of each tensor decode to exactly the official FP4 × E8M0 values;
  every other tensor equals a fresh conversion with the recipe.
- The file was renamed after conversion so that the name shows it is ELVEZ's; the contents were not changed.

## Compatibility

**Tested:**

- IXV's engine (`ixv-server`, IXV 1.17.4, runtime `fe3eccfc750d`), Metal backend, Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512 GB,
  `--ctx 131072 --batched-session 1 --warm-weights`, with the DSpark file (`--dspark`).
- With the vision encoder (`--vision`) the engine starts and loads it; we have not yet evaluated image answers with
  this file.

**Memory.** The engine keeps about 287 GiB resident (278.3 GiB of weights plus buffers and KV). The GPU driver counts
the resident model for each process, so two engines with this file (for example a main agent and a subagent) do not
fit in 512 GB, even though they share the file. IXV runs this file as the main agent with the standard Q2 as the
subagent: about 440–454 GiB wired in total, about 30 GiB left for other applications.

**Not tested:**

- Upstream antirez/ds4.
- llama.cpp or other GGUF runtimes. The architecture is `deepseek41`, and the Engram tables use a layout of our own.
- CUDA / ROCm, SSD streaming, tensor parallelism, other Apple Silicon generations, machines with less than 512 GB.

## Evaluation

One machine (Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512 GB), IXV 1.17.4 with the production settings (`--ctx 131072
--batched-session 1 --warm-weights`, DSpark on, no images). The standard Q2 was measured the day before with the
same engine, settings and script. Temperature 0, one run each.

### Speed (decode, 3 runs each, no prompt cache)

| Prompt | Standard Q2 | This file |
|---|---:|---:|
| Short Japanese prompt (27 tokens) | 46.0 tok/s | **42.5 tok/s** |
| ~6.3k-token prompt | 41.7 tok/s (prefill 9.6 s) | **39.5 tok/s** (prefill 9.0 s) |
| ~38.8k-token prompt | 36.8 tok/s (prefill 55.4 s) | **35.0 tok/s** (prefill 53.0 s) |

### Quality

| Test | Standard Q2 | This file |
|---|---:|---:|
| HumanEval, 164 problems (chat, thinking on, max 16,384 tokens, re-indented) | 152/164 (92.7%) | **162/164 (98.8%)** |
| Japanese knowledge QA, 48 questions (thinking off) | 46/48 | **46/48** (one more answer is correct in substance) |
| Japanese long-form writing, 6 prompts, max 4,096 tokens, judged by Claude, /20 | 13.0 | **16.0** |
| Number test, 20 questions (readings in 万・億 and others; tools on; read by hand) | 18/20 | **18/20** |

Notes on the quality results:

- **HumanEval.** All 162 answers with code passed. The 2 failures (problems 40 and 145) ended with no code: the
  model thought until the 16,384-token limit. The standard Q2 had 9 such problems and 3 wrong answers.
- **Long-form.** This file wrote 5 of the 6 prompts (scores 18, 20, 19, 20, 19); the standard Q2 wrote 4. The
  quality of the answered prompts is about the same. On the procedure-manual prompt both thought until the
  4,096-token limit and gave no text.
- **Numbers.** Both files misread the same kind of number (shifting a digit across 万), so we think this comes from
  the model rather than from quantization.
- The Japanese QA and long-form prompts and the number test are ELVEZ's internal evaluation sets and are not published.

## Limitations

- One machine, one evaluation session, one run each at temperature 0. Small test sets.
- Image answers, temperature 1.0 and long sessions are not yet evaluated.
- Needs about 287 GiB resident memory; see [Compatibility](#compatibility).
- This is not a release by DeepSeek or antirez. Please report problems with these files to us, not to them.

## 日本語の概要

- エルブズの AI開発ディストリビューション [IXV](https://ixv.jp/) が、Mac Studio でメインのモデルとして試している DeepSeek V4.1 Flash です。作り方と測ったことを誰でも確かめられるよう、ここで公開しています。
- DeepSeek の公式の重み `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` は、専門家を FP4 で持っています。このファイルは、その専門家を値を変えずに GGUF の MXFP4 の並びに置き換えたもので、専門家は劣化していません。エルブズの[標準の Q2](https://huggingface.co/elvezjp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ELVEZ-Q2-gguf) は、専門家を約 2.3 ビットに削っています。
- Mac Studio（M3 Ultra、512 GB）の IXV で、標準の Q2 と同じ条件で比べました。HumanEval 162/164（Q2 は 152/164）、日本語の長文 16.0（Q2 は 13.0）、日本語知識 QA と数字の試験は同じでした。生成は 5〜8% 遅く（毎秒 42.5 トークンなど）、メモリは約 287 GiB 要ります（Q2 は約 161 GiB）。
- 1つのファイルが Hugging Face の上限（500 GB）を超えるため、3つに分けて置いています。3つともダウンロードして `cat` でつなぎ、SHA-256 が上の表と同じことを確かめてください。
- 同じファイルのエンジンを2つ（メインとサブエージェントなど）動かすと、GPU のドライバが2つ分を数えるため、512 GB に入りません。IXV では、サブエージェントに標準の Q2 を使っています。
- 動作を確かめたのは IXV のエンジン（Metal、M3 Ultra）だけです。llama.cpp などの一般の GGUF の実行環境では動かない見込みです。
- ライセンスは元のモデルに合わせて MIT です。
